hints: Look at how saturation must change from 0% at 0 kPa to 97% at 14 kPa, and remember the oxygen dissociation curve is not a straight line, so check which row rises slowly, then fast, then slowly again.

Think about cooperative binding giving an S-shaped curve, so saturation should still be quite low at $2\text{ kPa}$, rise steeply around $4$ to $7\text{ kPa}$, then flatten near $93$ to $97\%$ by $12$ to $14\text{ kPa}$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the shape you expect**

Think of the adult oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve in your head. It starts at (0,0), stays low and flat at first, then shoots up steeply in the middle, then flattens off at the top near 100%.

That S-shape is due to cooperative binding: the first $O_2$ is hard to load, the next ones are easier, then the last sites are hard to fill.

**Set your start and end anchors**

You are told saturation is $0\%$ at $0\text{ kPa}$ and $97\%$ at $14\text{ kPa}$.

So at $2\text{ kPa}$ the value must still be low, and at $12\text{ kPa}$ it must already be very close to $97\%$, because the top of the curve is almost flat.

**Test the rows against the S-shape**

Only row C fits: $15\%$ at $2\text{ kPa}$ (low lag phase), then a big jump to $56\%$ at $4\text{ kPa}$ and $80\%$ at $7\text{ kPa}$ (steep middle), then only a small rise to $93\%$ at $12\text{ kPa}$ (flat top leading smoothly to $97\%$ at $14\text{ kPa}$).

The other rows are either far too low at the top or far too high at the start to make a proper S-shape.

options.A: Too low throughout and almost linear. $40\%$ at $12\text{ kPa}$ could never jump to $97\%$ by $14\text{ kPa}$ on a normal flattening curve.
options.B: Also too low at the top. $65\%$ at $12\text{ kPa}$ leaves an impossibly steep final rise to $97\%$ at $14\text{ kPa}$, and it lacks the clear steep middle and flat top.
options.C: Perfect S-shape. Low start, steep rise in the middle, then flattening to $93\%$ at $12\text{ kPa}$ which leads smoothly to $97\%$ at $14\text{ kPa}$.
options.D: Far too high at low partial pressure. $60\%$ saturated at only $2\text{ kPa}$ misses the low flat lag phase of cooperative binding.
